\[
T = m \left(1 + k \left(\frac{s}{R} - 1\right)\right),
\quad
I_{\text{out}} = \begin{cases} 255 & I > T \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},
\qquad k = 0.5,\ R = 128
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(m, s\): The local mean and standard deviation
- \(k\): The weight of the deviation term
- \(R\): The dynamic range of the standard deviation

m and s are the mean and the population standard deviation of the window around the pixel. Sauvola and Pietikainen use k = 0.5 and R = 128 for 8-bit images. Where the window is flat, s is small and T falls to about m (1 - k), well below the mean, so noise stays black. Where there is text, s is large and T moves toward m. The same formula is scikit-image's threshold_sauvola. For dark text on a light page, use Invert so the text becomes white. The result is 255 where the value is above the threshold and 0 elsewhere, or the reverse with Invert.
